sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the strongest driver of default risk: it accounts for about 38% of the model's importance, and risk rises sharply as utilization climbs, with the largest increase among applicants using most of their credit limit.
Past delinquencies are the second or third most important driver, and having at least one delinquency raises default risk compared with having none.
Income is the other leading driver, and higher income generally lowers default risk, with the effect strongest at the top of the income range.
Length of credit history is a weak effect, ranking among the less important features, and a longer history is associated with somewhat lower risk.
The data do not settle whether debt-to-income ratio, number of dependents, months at address and age matter, since their effects are too uncertain to separate from zero at this sample size.
Recent credit inquiries hardly matter for the model's predictions.
The interactions in the model are small, and none of the pairs we examined changes the picture of the main drivers.

The debt-to-income ratio has at most a moderate effect on default risk.
The number of dependents has at most a moderate effect on default risk.
Months at the current address has at most a moderate effect on default risk.
Age hardly matters for default risk.
The number of recent inquiries hardly matters for default risk.
